glossary.Benign: Not cancerous and not life-threatening, although it can still cause disability.
glossary.Oscillation: A regular back-and-forth rhythmic movement or electrical activity.
glossary.Bilateral: Affecting both sides of the body.
glossary.Voluntary movement: Movement the person chooses to make, such as reaching for a cup.
glossary.Laryngeal muscles: Muscles of the voice box that control the vocal cords and voice.
glossary.Voice tremor: A shaky, wavering voice caused by tremor of the laryngeal muscles.
glossary.Arms outstretched: Arms held straight out in front; a posture that brings out postural tremor.
glossary.Stimulants: Substances such as caffeine that increase nervous system activity and worsen tremor.
glossary.Depressants: Substances such as alcohol or benzodiazepines that dampen nervous system activity.
glossary.Functional impairment: Difficulty with everyday tasks such as writing, eating or drinking because of the illness.
glossary.Clinical diagnosis: A diagnosis made from history and examination alone, with no confirmatory test.
glossary.Gold standard: The best available way of confirming a diagnosis or treating a condition.
glossary.Thyroid disease: Over- or underactivity of the thyroid gland; an overactive thyroid can cause tremor.
glossary.Contraindicated: Should not be given because the risk of harm outweighs the benefit.
glossary.Asthma: Chronic airway disease with reversible narrowing; non-selective beta-blockers can trigger attacks.
glossary.Pathophysiology: The disturbed body processes that produce a disease.
glossary.Cerebellum: Back part of the brain that coordinates movement, balance and timing.
glossary.Thalamus: Relay station deep in the brain that passes signals between the cerebellum, basal ganglia and cortex.
glossary.Cortex: Outer layer of the brain; the motor cortex sends movement commands to muscles.
glossary.Olivary: Relating to the inferior olive in the brainstem, which sends timing signals to the cerebellum.
glossary.Dopaminergic: Using or relating to dopamine as a chemical messenger.
glossary.Muscle tone: The slight resting tension in a muscle that resists passive movement.
glossary.Physiological tremor: A tiny normal tremor everyone has, increased by adrenaline, anxiety, caffeine or fatigue.
glossary.Family history: Illness in blood relatives, suggesting an inherited cause.
glossary.Beta-blocker: Drug that blocks adrenaline's effect on beta receptors, slowing the heart and reducing tremor.
glossary.Caffeine: A stimulant found in coffee, tea and energy drinks that worsens essential tremor.
glossary.Head tremor: Rhythmic nodding or shaking of the head, also called titubation.
